questions.passage: The other interesting finding from the study was that functional distance also matters. Those who lived close to the staircases were far more likely to become friends with someone living on a different floor than those who lived farther away from the staircases. What this suggests is that physical and functional distance dictate the probability of a chance meeting, and that the more frequently one meets someone informally, the more likely it is that a friendship emerges.
questions.prompt: What does functional distance help explain here?
options: Why floor numbers alone perfectly predict every friendship.
Why everyone near stairs becomes friends immediately.
Why convenient routes can increase informal encounters and friendship opportunities.
Why physical distance ceases to matter near staircases.
questions.promptZh: 这里的功能距离帮助解释什么？
optionsZh: 仅靠楼层号码便能完美预测每段友谊。
为何楼梯旁的人马上全成朋友。
方便的动线为何增加非正式相遇与交友机会。
为何楼梯附近物理距离就无关紧要。
analyses: A 文中比较相遇机会，没有确定性预测。
B more likely 是概率而非必然，且没有立即的时限。
C 楼梯位置影响跨楼层接触，反复偶遇提高形成友谊可能性。
D physical and functional 表明两者都相关。这里是研究结果和机制解释，不是此片段中的随机曝光实验。

the more frequently one meets someone informally, the more likely it is that a friendship emerges.

questions.passage: Even before he conducted this series of experiments, Zajonc made an ingenious refinement of previous research on word frequency and its link to perceived “desirability” of a word (i.e., how good or bad a word sounds). questions.prompt: How was word desirability determined in the earlier work?
options: By counting printed occurrences without asking any speakers.
By measuring how long words took to pronounce.

questions.translation: 这些词频研究发现很有趣，但仍属相关性结果。也就是说，我们不能据此推断频率与喜欢某词之间的因果效应。因此 Zajonc 设计实验，向参与者呈现 iktitaf、afworbu、saricik 等无意义词。实验者称其为“土耳其语”词（其实不是），并教他们各词的发音。

evidence.quote: The findings from this research on word frequency are fascinating, but they are still correlational. That is, we cannot infer a causal effect between frequency and liking a word. So Zajonc designed an experiment in which participants were presented with nonsense words such as “iktitaf,” “afworbu,” and “saricik.” The experimenter told the participants that these were “Turkish” words (they weren’t) and showed them how to pronounce each.

He then replicated this initial finding with Chinese characters. In the next experiment, Zajonc used photos of graduating Michigan State University seniors and replicated again that those same photos were better liked when presented more frequently to the participants than when they were presented less frequently.

All photographs received identical ratings.
Only real words benefited from repetition.
More frequent presentation increased positive evaluations of the same stimuli.
questions.promptZh: 不同材料中重复出现什么结果模式？
optionsZh: 汉字总比照片受欢迎。
所有照片评分相同。
只有真实词重复后才受益。
同一刺激呈现更频繁时，正面评价更高。
analyses: A 没有汉字与照片之间的偏好排名。
